critic.fix_suggestion: Modify the 'front cylinder' geometry of the upper deck hump to increase its length, radial thickness, and vertical scale. Specifically: 1) Extend the longitudinal length by a factor of 1.5x to reach further back along the fuselage; 2) Increase the radial diameter by 30% to widen the cabin profile; 3) Scale the height vertically by 20% to create a more prominent 'double-decker' silhouette. Finally, apply a 45-degree taper/fillet at the junction where the cylinder meets the main fuselage to smooth the transition from the body diameter.

discrepancies.observed: The upper deck hump ends very close to the cockpit area.
discrepancies.reference: The hump extends significantly further back along the fuselage.

discrepancies.observed: A sharp, abrupt transition from the main fuselage diameter to the hump.
discrepancies.reference: A smooth, gradual blending between the upper deck and the main body.

discrepancies.observed: The top of the hump is relatively low compared to the nose.
discrepancies.reference: The hump creates a distinct high-profile 'double-decker' look at the front.
discrepancies.direction_of_fix: increase vertical scale of upper cylinder

discrepancies.observed: The hump appears narrow and thin relative to the fuselage diameter.
discrepancies.reference: The hump is wide enough to accommodate a full cabin row.
discrepancies.direction_of_fix: increase radial thickness of front cylinder
